mainEntity.name: Which one-rep max formula is most accurate?

acceptedAnswer.text: No single formula wins for every lift and person. Results are closest together for low-rep sets, which is why using a set of 3–6 reps and averaging the formulas gives a steadier estimate.

mainEntity.name: How many reps should I use to estimate my 1RM?

acceptedAnswer.text: A hard set of about 3–10 reps works best. Above 10–12 reps, the formulas diverge and become less reliable, because endurance starts to limit the set more than strength.

mainEntity.name: How often should I re-test my 1RM?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every 4–8 weeks is common. Re-estimating from a recent hard set is safer than a true max attempt and keeps your training percentages up to date.
